chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salamah ibn al-Khattab, from 'Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Tatari, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ibn Muskan, from Shurahbil al-Kindi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

He was asked, “How does a menstruating woman know her purification?” He said: “She should brace herself with her left leg against the wall and insert the cotton with her right hand; then if there appears on the cotton something like the head of a fly...”

key_terms.الْحَائِطِ: the wall against which she braces herself
key_terms.الْكُرْسُفَ: cotton used for checking for blood
key_terms.رَأْسِ الذُّبَابِ: the head of a fly, used here as a measure of a very small amount
key_terms.طُهْرَهَا: her state of purity after menstruation

ai.seo_question: How does a menstruating woman determine that she has become pure according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a legal method for determining whether menstrual bleeding has ceased and purity has been attained. It belongs to the jurisprudence of ritual purity and provides practical guidance related to the signs by which a woman assesses the end of hayd.
